findings.text: Traversal over an address interval visits populated levels depth first with per level entry callbacks and a hole report for empty entries. Install mode allocates missing intermediate tables instead of reporting holes. A handler can request reexamination of the current entry or skipping of its subtree or default descent, with retry used after concurrent table changes or missing mappings.

Descent below a level occurs only when a deeper entry handler or install capability is present. When only installation is active, present huge entries at PUD and PMD are left intact rather than split. Without an associated mapping, leaf or absent entries end that branch. With a mapping, huge entries are split before descending to PTEs.

Reported hole depth collapses folded levels. A level whose table contains a single entry is reported at the next lower depth, so callers observe compact depth numbering independent of configuration folding.

Creation of P4D and PUD and PMD tables is serialized by the owning address space table lock, with PMD creation using the PUD derived lock. Concurrent creation retains the winner and releases the loser, with ordering enforced between table initialization and publication. Successful insertion of new PUD and PMD tables increments the address space table counters.

The intermediate and leaf table allocation helpers report resource exhaustion without side effects and otherwise ensure the child table exists on return, tolerating concurrent population by another thread.

PTE traversal supports a lockless mode for kernel mappings and a locked mode for ordinary mappings, distinguishing kernel and user address handling and pairing each mapping acquisition with its matching release. Empty PTEs are filled through the install callback with cache maintenance for mapped operations, while populated entries use the entry callback. Absence of a mapping requests reexamination.
Installation of PTEs through the walker is reserved for internal memory management use and is rejected as unsafe for exported traversal interfaces.

A huge folio is eligible for vmemmap reduction only when not already reduced and when the global optimization switch is enabled and when its type has a positive reducible size. Reducible size is the total descriptor memory for the huge page minus a fixed reserve, forced to zero when the descriptor size is not a power of two. One build variant always reports zero reducible size.

Shared vmemmap tail descriptors are cached per zone and order and initialized as compound tails with unmapped count and node and zone identity and tail mapping marker and head linkage. Concurrent creation retains a single winner and releases the loser.

Returning unused reservations always decrements the reservation count, then releases at most the surplus portion evenly across memory nodes until the pool is exhausted, deferring actual page release to a bulk path that temporarily drops the hugetlb lock. Gigantic types without runtime support stop after accounting.

Bulk release first restores full descriptors for all queued folios. On failure it frees whatever progress allows and retries until restoration succeeds, then clears hugetlb identity under lock only for restored folios before releasing each folio with scheduling opportunity.

Release of a huge folio is synchronous except that an optimized folio in atomic context is queued to a deferred work list when the queue transitions from empty. Gigantic types without runtime support and folios with unreliable poison tracking are intentionally retained. Failed descriptor restoration requeues the folio as surplus. Otherwise hugetlb identity is cleared under lock and poison state is migrated to raw error pages and the frozen range is returned through CMA or the buddy allocator with an expectation of no remaining references.

Insertion of a folio into the hugetlb pool requires the hugetlb lock and an optimized descriptor state, reinitializes queue linkage, increments total and per node pool counts with optional surplus accounting, reestablishes hugetlb identity after clearing private data, refreshes architecture flags, and enqueues the folio for allocation.

Restoration of full descriptors is a no operation for nonreduced folios and for builds without reduction support. Otherwise the range covering the folio descriptors beyond the head reserve is repopulated from newly allocated single pages drawn from the range node with retry tolerant allocation, with full cleanup of the provisional list on exhaustion, followed by remapping that clears the reduced state on success.

Hardware poison state for huge folios is tracked in a lock free list anchored in the folio, with unreliable tracking and reduced descriptors blocking unpoisoning and release. Draining the list either propagates poison to member pages or decrements the global and block poison counts while freeing tracking records, returning the number of records processed.
Huge page allocation honors only bind mode task policy whose zone and cpuset constraints are satisfied, otherwise proceeding without a policy nodemask.

The walker tolerates concurrent table reclamation and splitting by reexamining entries whose type changed between sampling and descent, and the PTE leaf path validates mapping state. Hugetlb bulk paths tolerate allocation failure during descriptor restoration by partial progress and retry rather than loss.

Hugetlb pool accounting and queue manipulation require the hugetlb interrupt safe lock, with bulk release temporarily dropping it across operations that may allocate or schedule and reacquiring it afterwards, and with identity clearing performed under the same lock.

Several huge page helpers have build variants that are intentional no operations returning neutral values, disabling vmemmap reduction and CMA release and raw poison tracking when the corresponding feature is not enabled.
